principles: A gate must never manufacture the violation it is checking for: a duplicate identity may only come from the recorded evidence, never from a helper that rewrote it.
Fix the mechanism that fabricates the false signal, not the check that reports it, so the genuine double-vote protection keeps its full strength.
Preserve the existing benign behaviour exactly: unrelated whole-tree drift must still be accepted with its re-attestation advisory.
A wedge whose only escape is a human-gated override is a defect, because ordinary parallel development reaches it and the escape is not discoverable.
drivers: B-4043 lost hours to an unreachable DONE and was rescued only by an accidental storyFilesHash change.
Any story that submits a quorum at two materials sharing one storyFilesHash reaches the same wedge.
The reproduction already exists and isolates the cause, so the fix can be verified red-to-green immediately.

options.name: A-skip-colliding-downgrade
pros: Smallest change, one precondition in the helper that creates the collision
Both existing mechanisms keep their semantics
Advisory path for genuine drift is untouched
Directly turns the existing red test green
cons: Needs the helper to know how host identity is compared, duplicating a little of groupByIndependentHost's notion of identity

options.name: B-round-scoped-runids
pros: Round-scoped quorum runIds would make the gate's own prescribed remedy (a fresh review round) actually work
cons: Changes the quorum identity scheme and every consumer assuming the fixed -q-r1..r3 names
Much larger blast radius for a bug that has one narrow cause
Does not stop the downgrade from fabricating duplicates in other runId spaces

options.name: C-grouping-prefers-newest
pros: A single change in the grouping would cover every producer of colliding verdicts
cons: Silently preferring the newest verdict per identity weakens the real double-vote check
Turns an integrity signal into a resolution heuristic

options.name: D-rely-on-human-fallback
pros: No code change; the human-gated fallback already exists
cons: Leaves a reachable wedge in ordinary parallel development
The escape requires a human signature that the owner session is explicitly forbidden to make

rationale: Option A-skip-colliding-downgrade removes the fabrication at its source with the smallest blast radius: the downgrade simply declines to rewrite a superseded verdict onto the current material when an identity-equal verdict is already there natively. Both the drift allowance and the double-vote check keep their exact semantics, the advisory still fires for genuine drift, and the already-written red test flips from 0/3 to 3/3 as the proof. B-round-scoped-runids and C-grouping-prefers-newest were rejected for changing the identity scheme and for weakening a real integrity check respectively; D-rely-on-human-fallback was rejected because the wedge is reachable by ordinary work.

preMortem.scenario: The precondition is written so broadly that it also suppresses a genuine double vote recorded twice at the current material.
preMortem.trigger: Red test passes but the double-vote protection silently stops firing.
preMortem.consequence: A real integrity check is disabled while looking green.
preMortem.mitigation: Only skip the rewrite for verdicts whose materialDigest is NOT already the current one; verdicts recorded natively at the current material are never touched by the downgrade, so genuine duplicates there still collide.

preMortem.scenario: The helper's notion of identity drifts from groupByIndependentHost, so a collision the grouping would flag is not detected by the precondition.
preMortem.trigger: A verdict pair sharing only sessionId (not hostId) still gets rewritten and re-collides.
preMortem.consequence: The wedge returns in a narrower form and the red test does not catch it.
preMortem.mitigation: Match on the same triple the grouping unions on (hostId/sessionId/keyId, any-field overlap), and state that coupling in a comment next to both sites.

preMortem.scenario: Suppressing the rewrite hides a case where the superseded verdict was the ONLY evidence for that round.
preMortem.trigger: A round that used to count via a downgraded verdict now reports missing hosts.
preMortem.consequence: A story that previously passed the floor starts failing it.
preMortem.mitigation: Skip only when an identity-equal verdict already exists natively at the current material, i.e. exactly the case where the downgraded copy adds nothing; a lone superseded verdict is still downgraded and still counts.
